## Learning goals

By the end of this page:

- I will be able to move from a real situation to a testable idea.
- I will be able to use evidence and feedback to decide what to change.

This is important because a good project solves a real need and improves through testing.

Start with the situation, move through N.I.C.E., and repeat the process after evaluation. Each step produces something useful for the next step.

## Situation: understand what is happening

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p3" alt="Situation step of the N.I.C.E. design process, separating facts, assumptions, and interpretations" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Separate what is known from what still needs to be checked. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Before choosing a solution, describe the real situation.

- **Facts** can be observed or supported with evidence.
- **Assumptions** may be true, but still need to be checked.
- **Interpretations** are what you think the facts mean. They can change when you learn more.

The result is a clear situation statement that does not jump ahead to a product or solution.

[Use the N.I.C.E. Needs Worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/edit) to record the situation, users, facts, assumptions, questions, and restrictions.

## N: Needs and Necessities

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p4" alt="Needs and Necessities step of the N.I.C.E. design process" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Define what the solution must accomplish before deciding what to make. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Turn the situation into requirements.

- A **need** describes what the solution should accomplish.
- A **necessity** is a requirement that must be met.
- A **nice-to-have** would improve the solution but is not essential.
- **Priorities** show which requirements matter most.

The result is a clear need statement and a prioritized list of requirements. Describe the function you need, not a product you have already decided to build.

[Continue in the N.I.C.E. Needs Worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ObkJz3sYVXwB9VkNUiybXZGZ-ihuGw1FarRj81LtAo/edit) to write the need statement and rank the necessities and nice-to-haves.

## I: Investigate and Inquire

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p5" alt="Investigate and Inquire step of the N.I.C.E. design process" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Research begins with questions and comparison, not a random search. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Find out what already exists and what the evidence suggests.

1. What do we need?
2. What solutions already exist?
3. What could work for this situation?
4. What should be improved, combined, simplified, or changed?

Compare each idea with the needs, necessities, and priorities. The result is an evidence-based direction and a reason for choosing it.

[Use the N.I.C.E. Inquiry Worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c-7TbI3IMOicnHsTUSLkGNJ4s1i2OA6d458S2bTZ2ho/edit) to ask questions, compare existing solutions, and decide what to adapt.

## C: Create and Communicate

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p6" alt="Create and Communicate step of the N.I.C.E. design process" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Make the idea visible, explain it clearly, and ask for useful feedback. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Create a sketch, model, prototype, or other representation that lets someone understand the idea. Explain the situation, the need, and how the idea helps. Then ask specific questions instead of only asking, “Do you like it?”

A short pitch can follow this sequence:

1. Have you ever experienced this situation?
2. Have you needed or wanted this improvement?
3. Our idea is… It helps by…

The result is a clear pitch, useful feedback, and one specific change to consider.

Use the communication worksheets in order:

1. [Communicate Worksheet Online](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T6f3beZhKXiOxS1ecXt3FHbam2yOqeP1yXrmaLFSbAs/edit) or [Pitch and Show Your Idea Print](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F_7NWcW4Bzd-PE7BdLssdBxeT-49clS92381QXjW8gw/edit) to explain and show the idea.
2. [Feedback Package](https://docs.google.com/document/d/173eivGi-7of6WWqpPsK81p4Z2Q6_3fIiW5ffjRI6jRQ/edit) to collect specific feedback and find patterns.
3. [Plan and Plan Feedback](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QWY7ss3aY5wHh4ETOcSDGZxgpkrrIXcCYnWlXNv1lxo/edit) to identify resources, roles, steps, and improvements to the plan.

## E: Evaluate

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p7" alt="Evaluate step of the N.I.C.E. design process" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Use evidence to decide what to keep, change, remove, or test next. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Compare the idea or prototype with the original situation and the prioritized requirements. Check whether earlier assumptions were correct. Look for patterns in testing and feedback rather than reacting to one random comment.

Decide what to keep, change, remove, or test next. The result is a revised solution supported by evidence and reasons.

[Use the N.I.C.E. Evaluate Worksheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O_j4gcsUT0ELFpgJk3GiyG6B1l5brKPko-6lO8HQPfk/edit) to connect the feedback to a justified next change.

## Repeat the cycle

<figure>
  <img src="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ/export/png?id=1bQBt0WHBp6ca0RWtQHBHKbfqhzXMc4q4uUOJ8hHxvIQ&amp;pageid=p9" alt="Repeat the N.I.C.E. design-process cycle after evaluation" style="display:block;max-width:960px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption>Evaluation leads to the next version, not simply the end of the project. Figure from the class slide deck.</figcaption>
</figure>

Return to the needs after evaluation. Ask what the evidence proved, which assumption was wrong, which requirement matters most now, and what the next version should change. Design improves through these repeated, evidence-based decisions.

[Use the N.I.C.E. Design Log](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sai4_cQGkNudnAsLRYuwec6D-B-U4BqA8CCk0Nyo0CA/edit) to keep the worksheets, sketches, feedback, decisions, and later versions together.
